claim_en: GORING = HORN: ki yigach is the horn-act only; yigach (man-victim) vs yigof (21:35, beast-victim) split as act-word vs effect-word — a man has mazal (heavenly protection), so what fells a beast need not fell a man; hence mu'ad-for-beasts is NOT mu'ad-for-man (the reverse holds).
source: TT 28 (B1); Hirsch 21:35 (B20); Rashi/Shabbat 53b relay; MdRShbY

claim_en: GUILT ATTACHES TO THE ANIMAL: 'shor' 7x — woman's, orphans', guardian's, Temple's, WILDERNESS/ownerless, dead convert's ox all stoned; every species via shor-shor from Shabbat (the stoned ROOSTER of Jerusalem, Niddah 8a); counter-tradition preserved: R. Yehudah exempts the ownerless (Tosefta BK 4:6). Covenant ground: Gen 9:5 'from every beast I will demand it' — the stoning is delegated divine judgment (Noahide layer), not owner-punishment or police safety.
source: TT (B1 shor-shor-shiv'ah); Niddah 8a (B6); Tosefta BK 4:5-6 (B4); Ramban Gen 9:5 (B9); Hirsch 21:28 (B19)

claim_en: THE OX GETS THE COURT, NOT THE MERCIES: full capital process — 23 judges, verdict only in the ox's PRESENCE (ve-hu'ad be-va'alav = no testimony absent the party; exported to civil document-authentication BK 112b), terefah-ox exempt, 'as the owner's death so the ox's death' — but all ten acquittal-protections absent: the ox convicts by ONE vote. The Yerushalmi files the whole institution as decree: 'the stoned ox is entirely money — its stoning is gezerat ha-katuv.'
source: TT (B1 due-process battery); BK 112b (B5); R. Abbahu (B2); Yer.San 1:1 R. Yosi b'r Bun (B6)

claim_en: INTENT CONDITIONS: et ish — the ox must intend THIS victim (MdRShbY); aimed-at-beast-killed-man exempt, aimed-at-Shimon-killed-Reuven liable (transferred intent bounded by the particle et); the GOADED/stadium ox is not stoned (ki yigach — 'when IT gores', not when they make it gore) yet stays barred from the altar; Rambam promotes the coercion-exemption: the stadium killer-ox is KOSHER for sacrifice ('as one coerced').
source: MdRShbY (B3); Or HaChaim 21:28 + San 79a (B16-17); Gur Aryeh via BK 39a (B13); MT Issurei Mizbeach 4:3 (B7)

claim_en: THE BENEFIT-BAN RIDES THE VERDICT: prohibition lands at gmar din (sentencing), not the stoning — verdict dissolved after execution → carcass permitted; dissolved before → the ox returns to the herd (Keritot 6:2); slaughter-after-verdict stays forbidden; ET besaro sweeps in the hide (substance-and-accident ribbui; Malbim: et after a passive verb parses only as 'WITH its hide'); dung permitted; Shimon HaAmsoni's whole et-quantifier crisis anchors on this clause (BK 41b).
source: Mishnah Keritot 6:2 (B4); Gur Aryeh (B12); Malbim (B14); BK 41b (B5); TT (B1); Imrei HaTzvi verdict-carries-issur (B17)

claim_en: BAAL HASHOR NAKI: the tam's owner is clear even in Heaven's court (R. Yehudah); Meshekh Chokhmah on the missing 'ish': an ownerless or hekdesh ox is also stoned, so 'naki' must address whoever ACQUIRES the ox after the goring — the benefit-prohibition binds all persons, not just the owner.
source: TT (B1); Meshekh Chokhmah 21:28 (B16)

claim_en: THE FOREWARNED-STATE MACHINE WITH HYSTERESIS: escalation tam→mu'ad needs 3 gorings on 3 DAYS (R. Yehudah; R. Meir: 3 events); REVERSION needs only ONE day of children petting it un-gored — acquiring a habit is slow, breaking it is proof (TT grounds the asymmetry in habit-psychology and exports the one-day cessation standard to rescue Maharam of Rothenburg's 90-repetition liturgy rule). Forewarning is CONTEXT-INDEXED: mu'ad for Sabbaths only (reverts after 3 clean Sabbaths), mu'ad per species (ox+donkey+camel → mu'ad for all), and escalation can run on assessed PURSUITS with no completed goring.
source: TT 29 (B1); Tosefta BK 4:5 (B4); Chagigah 4a (B6); Yer.BK 4:2 (B5)

claim_en: THE FIVE WRITTEN TAM/MU'AD DIFFERENCES (the Mekhilta's block): (1) witnesses-and-warning required; (2) kofer only for mu'ad; (3) the 30-shekel slave fine only for mu'ad; (4) full vs half damage; (5) payment from the ESTATE (aliyyah) vs from the BODY of the ox — plus the unwritten sixth: the tam's half-damage is a FINE (kenas), so confession exempts it.
source: Mekhilta via TT 29 (B1); Ketubot 41a (B4)

claim_en: TWO EVIDENTIARY REGIMES IN TWO WORDS: ox-kills-MAN says ve-hu'ad be-va'alav — capital-style process (no circumstantial inference, testimony in the owner's presence, the ox's death hekesh'd to the owner's); ox-kills-OX says o noda — money-style process (R. Acha's camel-among-camels umdena and absent-party testimony suffice).
source: Meshekh Chokhmah Mishpatim (B16)

claim_en: VE-GAM BE'ALAV YUMAT = DEATH BY HEAVEN — the Gra's radical filing: 'the halakhah UPROOTS the verse' (halakhah okeret et ha-mikra); the peshat kept alive beside it: the unguarded mu'ad-owner is a murderer-in-formation (Netziv — Heaven will steer a killing to his hand); RYbZ's double answer to Agnatos the general (exoteric: a bandit's accomplice is as the bandit; esoteric: the 23-court isomorphism); and the blood-avenger who kills the OX-OWNER is himself a murderer — the go'el's license covers hands-on killers only.
source: Gra (B11); Netziv 21:29 (B14); Yer. via B6; Or HaChaim (B17); Targum Jonathan 'death from Heaven' (B7)

claim_en: GUARDING GRADES BY GRAMMAR: the BOUND suffix (ve-lo yishmerennu) = the reduced general guarding — which SUFFICES for the mu'ad (R. Yehudah, BK 45b: the notorious ox 'has a voice' and is avoided), so the tam ironically needs stricter guarding; tied-and-locked yet escaped → the mu'ad increment is exempt, the tam layer still pays; the DOUBLED ve-lo yishmerennu (21:29+36) pins liability on the owner IN PERSON even when his guard guarded perfectly — Malbim's Mekhilta rescue of Rambam Nizkei Mamon 4:4 against Raavad/Tur/Bach; owner-continuity: gored then consecrated/made ownerless → exempt (death, arraignment, verdict must run under ONE owner).
source: HaKtav VeHaKabbalah suffix-theory (B13); BK 45b; Malbim 21:29 (B15); TT (B1)

claim_en: KOFER MECHANICS: the 'im' is obligation, not option; payable only AFTER the victim dies; FULL kofer from EACH partner (atonement cannot halve — contrast the theft fine's five half-oxen); value = the VICTIM's worth (peshat: pidyon nafsho; machloket: the payer's); it is atonement that is ALSO a collectible debt — R. Yishmael: 'come and see the mercies — a man PURCHASES HIMSELF from Heaven's hand with money'; Ramban files it as sacrifice-like (court may not compel; Rambam: they distrain); Netziv: teshuvah, fasting, charity ride on top of the money; the woman's kofer goes to HER heirs, not the husband (kofer pays only after death = an expectancy, and husbands do not inherit expectancies); heirs may refuse as beneath their dignity (the 'assessed like a slave' shame), hence the im.
source: TT 30 (B1); Mekhilta; Ramban via Malbim (B15); Netziv (B14); Bekhor Shor + Chizkuni heirs'-option (B10); Or HaChaim partners-plural (B17)

claim_en: THE KOFER BOUNDARY: ransom is for the OWNER'S NEGLIGENCE, never for a killing act — no kofer for the human murderer (Num 35:31-32's explicit ban), and no kofer category exists for the pit-death (money cannot reach a human life the digger took; the guilt 'remains before the Presence of God' — the MISSING payment read as the GREATER culpability); the unintentional killing decouples everything on Resh Lakish's rule: no stoning → no 30-shekel fine and no kofer ('while the ox is under stoning the owner pays') vs R. Yochanan's im-ribbui.
source: Num 35:31 (patch pair); Hirsch 21:33 (B19); Resh Lakish + Rabbah BK 43a (B5)

claim_en: SON OR DAUGHTER: no vicarious liability in either direction — ka-mishpat ha-zeh ye'aseh lo: the SAME din when the victim is a minor (the ox/owner judged, never children punished for parents — the clause Ezek 18 doctrinalizes); includes the tumtum and androginos (the o read as doubt), one's own son and daughter, and the heirless convert; the contributory negligence of children who TEASE mad oxen is weighed (BK 24b) and overridden.
source: Yalkut 341:2 (B21); Malbim (B15); Netziv (B14); MdRShbY

claim_en: THE THIRTY: flat statutory tariff for the gored slave (Targum Jonathan: the CANAANITE slave), paid to the master, mu'ad-only, and payable even ABOVE the slave's market worth — it is kapparah, not damage-pricing; the half-slave killed draws HALF KENAS (15 to the master) + half kofer to his heirs — one person, both tracks; for a wife's melog-slave the thirty goes TO HER: le-adonav means the BODY's owner, and body-ownership beats fruit-ownership; Rambam's completion: a tam killing a slave unintentionally pays half his VALUE from its body 'as if it killed his ox.'
source: TT 32; Targum Jonathan (B7); Gur Aryeh kapparah (B12); Gittin 42a (B6); Malbim BK 89b-90 (B15); MT Nizkei Mamon 10:14 (B6)

claim_en: SIX RATIONALES OF THE FLAT 30, STACKED: frequency + litigation-cost (slaves live among the cattle — suits would multiply; Chizkuni; Bekhor Shor's 'so they won't come to quarrel'); the MIDDLE Arakhin valuation = the statutory average man (Bartenura); the adult-WOMAN's Arakhin station the slave shares (Maharal); a viciousness-fine — the superfluous ha-shor: it gored its daily stall-companion (Netziv); the shepherd's WAGE (the gored slave is the herd's shepherd; Zech 11:12's thirty); and Hirsch's crown: human life has NO market price — pricing the slave by actual worth would make the degrading valuation REAL, so the Torah fixes the sum at the HIGHEST woman's erekh, protecting 'the godlike value of every human life.' Erekh vs damim = two value-ontologies formally split.
source: Chizkuni (B10); Bekhor Shor (B11); Bartenura + Maharal + Da'at Zekenim gematria (B12); Netziv (B14); Hadar Zekenim/Zech 11:12 (B14); Hirsch (B19-20)

claim_en: THE TARIFF AS THE CANON'S SLAVE-PRICE CONSTANT: converted to thirty MITHQALS (Saadia), half a Cologne ounce (Rashi), esterlins with R. Tam's gold-doubles theory (harmonizing Araunah's 50 gold = 600 silver); recycled as the severance-grant floor of 30 sela (MT Slaves 3:14 — block-1 crossover); bid as the golden-calf ransom ('they exchanged His Glory for an OX — each owes the slave-tariff'; God rules: half a shekel); Joseph's 300 to Benjamin = 10 × 30, the Gittin tenfold fine for selling a slave to gentiles.
source: Tafsir Rasag (B21); Rashi (B8); Hadar Zekenim + Levush (B14); MT Avadim 3:14 (B7); Tanchuma Ki Tisa 6 (B8); Chizkuni + Bahya Gen 45:22 (B10)

claim_en: THE PIT'S DEPTH LAW HANGS ON A MISSING WORD: every damage clause writes 'and it dies' EXCEPT the pit — so there EXISTS a pit liable without death, and WHICH (nine handbreadths injury-only vs ten death) was 'handed over to the sages' (Meshekh Chokhmah: 'the depth of the peshat'); digger-after-digger: the COMPLETER of the tenth handbreadth pays — read from plene/defective spelling (bor full = the 10-pit, bar defective = the 9-pit, ba'al ha-BOR full again = 'he who fills pays' — the Gra) and from verb choice (karah = begin/modify, chafar = finish — Mecklenburg, Netziv, Malbim, Hirsch independently); the hevel-vs-chavata physics (vapor-pit needs 10; impact-pit six suffice, 'the ox's belly rides four off the ground') encoded in the same orthography.
source: Meshekh Chokhmah (B16); Gra via HaKtav VeHaKabbalah (B2, B13); Malbim/Netziv/Mecklenburg/Hirsch (B13-15, B19); R. Shlomo Cohen via PY (B17); BK 50b-51a

claim_en: THE PIT'S EXCLUSIONS ARE DECREE: shor ve-lo adam, chamor ve-lo kelim (a MAN or VESSELS in the pit draw no money remedy) — and Mizrachi proves it is gezerat ha-katuv, not wisdom ('a man has sense' fails: the senseless child, the blind, the night-faller are excluded too); Ralbag's structure-as-law: the pit-clause INTERRUPTS ox-kills-man before ox-kills-ox and omits any man's death — exclusion by architecture; the pit is measured by its VICTIM ('the fill of the faller — even a chicken'); the public-domain pit is one of Scripture's two ownership-FICTIONS ('made his' for liability, with afternoon chametz); karka olam causation: fell OUTSIDE the pit — the world's ground hurt it, exempt; INSIDE — the pit-bottom 'received its dangerous properties through him.'
source: Mizrachi (B16); Ralbag shoresh 3 (B18); Yer.BK 1:2 R. Elazar HaKappar (B5); Rav Giddel fiction-pair (B16); Hirsch (B19); Paaneach Raza ordering (B26)

claim_en: COVER LAW + GUARDING ECONOMY: ve-lo yechasennu — the consequence-clause (ba'al ha-bor yeshallem) proves covering is REQUIRED (the lo-parser paradigm: Rambam's Shorashim test-case; Zevachim 66a uses our clause to discipline Leviticus readings); a PROPER cover exempts even if it rotted from within (SA CM 410:22); dug-and-HANDED-TO-THE-PUBLIC → exempt (Nechunya the ditch-digger — 'he fulfilled this law and it stands', with his theodicy: exacting to a hairsbreadth); the pit sits among the FOUR MINIMIZED GUARDINGS (a cover suffices — the guarding-economy of the whole damage system).
source: Rambam Shorashim 8:5 (B7); Zevachim 66a (B22); SA CM 410:22 (B21); Yalkut 341:17 Nechunya (B21); Yalkut 341:8 (B21); Rashbam working-digger realism (B19)

claim_en: OWNERSHIP OF A HOLE: pit-liability transfers to buyer and donee but NOT the heir — pure liability with no substance admits no yerushah (the Rogatchover on Rambam's omitted word); the liability survives the digger's DEATH toward the public (Ben Ish Hai's sin-innovator pit: 'though he has died, later generations' corruption is charged to him' — collected from best land: 'not the mouse steals, but the hole'); ba'al ha-bor and shallem yeshallem are UNGENDERED — the block's torts bind both sexes (R. Yonatan's route; R. Yoshiyah derives it from Num 5).
source: Tzafnat Pa'neach (B21); Ben Ish Hai (B11); Yalkut 701:2 (B22)

claim_en: VE-HA-MET YIHYEH LO — THE CARCASS: halakhah gives it to the VICTIM (counted into the damages); the peshat gives it to the DAMAGER ('since he pays full value, justice is that the dead be his') — Rashbam and the Gra state the split OPENLY, both readings on the page; Ralbag's anti-spoilage economics: vest it in the victim AT DEATH so someone sells it before it rots (possession=admission would freeze both parties), and the pit-owner still pays the hauling; Tosafot takes LEXICON from the clause: a beast is called met but never nefesh met — pit-grammar deciding nazir law.
source: Rashbam + Gra (B11, B19); Ralbag (B18); Tosafot Nazir 48a (B21); Netinah LaGer on Onkelos 'the VALUE of the dead' (B16)

claim_en: THE TAM SPLIT: sell the LIVE ox and halve money and carcass — valid ONLY between EQUAL-value oxen ('the Torah spoke only when the two are equal' — else the tam pays more than the harm or the damager profits, both barred); the three-case table: 100 gores 200 → the victim takes the WHOLE gorer; 200 gores 100 → a quarter; equals → half (R. Akiva to R. Meir: 'read the whole verse'); the no-profit fence: shallem yeshallem — owners PAY, owners never COLLECT (R. Yehudah's carcass-appreciation cap); Mecklenburg reads the Mishnah out of one word: ve-GAM = the LOSS (root gamam, 'the loss on the dead they halve' = pechat she-pichato mitah machatzin verbatim), ve-chatzu = unequal division, yechetzuN's paragogic nun = exact halves — and that nun carries the law by PERSONS not locality (half-damage even on the victim's premises, BK 26a).
source: MdRShbY (B3); Yalkut 341:19+22 (B22); Mecklenburg (B13); Malbim ethology + machatzit semantics (B15); Hirsch nun (B20)

claim_en: HALF-DAMAGE PHILOSOPHY AND ENFORCEMENT GEOGRAPHY: Rav Papa — it is MONEY (oxen presumed unguarded; the Torah PITIED the not-yet-warned owner); Rav Huna b. R. Yehoshua — it is a FINE (oxen presumed guarded; he owes nothing, the Torah fined him to make him guard); halakhah = FINE → palga nizka is NOT collected in Babylonia (fines need ordination) — but the victim's SEIZURE stands, the damager can be summoned to the Land, and he is EXCOMMUNICATED until the hazard is removed (R. Natan's rule: no bad dog, no shaky ladder — 'place no blood in your house').
source: Ketubot 41a (B4); Yalkut 341:21 (B22); Lekach Tov + R. Natan (B8)

claim_en: THE REMEDY RESHAPES OWNERSHIP: the tam's from-the-body payment makes victim and damager PARTNERS in the living ox (R. Akiva — the victim's consecration of it takes effect; Ralbag: the victim-partner shares liability for the NEXT goring in proportion); Netziv: the verse orders SALE-and-split rather than co-ownership — no forced partnership with your damager; Hirsch's moral-hazard traffic law: full compensation would make owners careless ('fully insured, they might even try to have them injured'), so the street places any two meeting animals 'under the combined care of the two owners' — the basis of the rights of open traffic.
source: R. Akiva halakha (B2); Ralbag co-defendant (B18); Netziv (B14); Hirsch 21:35 (B20)

claim_en: THE MU'AD PAYS IN FULL FROM THE BEST: shallem yeshallem shor tachat ha-shor — full damage from meitav (Bekhor Shor's collections essay: damages from BEST land, loans from worst — incentive design); the carcass still offsets (ve-ha-met yihyeh lo again); OWNERSHIP MUST PERSIST goring→judgment: the superfluous be'alav teaches an ox made ownerless after goring is exempt from damages though still stoned (R. Akiva Eiger's paradox — the capital verdict itself makes it ownerless — answered from the Shitah: collect from the condemned ox's own PLOW-EARNINGS while it waits).
source: Bekhor Shor 21:34 meitav (B11); Rosh + R. Akiva Eiger + Shitah Mekubetzet (B13)

claim_en: THE HEKDESH AND GENTILE ASYMMETRIES: hekdesh ox gores a commoner's → EXEMPT; commoner's gores hekdesh → FULL even as tam (R. Shimon b. Menasya) — while damage TO hekdesh has NO earthly claimant at all (Hirsch's anti-hierarchy proof: 'anybody could demolish the whole Temple treasure without finding any judge empowered to make him pay one penny' — a priestly forgery would have avenged its own sanctuary; the law's indifference is its authorship-proof); re'ehu forfeiture doctrine: the gentile asymmetry grounded in the Noahide laws unkept (R. Abbahu's 'He saw and released the nations'; MdRShbY's Paran twin) — nations that KEEP the seven are judged as Israel (Rambam Nizkei Mamon 5:5: 'we judge them by THEIR OWN laws'; TT: 'most nations of this time have law with us as Israel's law').
source: Yalkut 345:1 (B22); Hirsch 21:36 (B20); MdRShbY (B3); TT re'ehu apologia (B2); Rambam via PY (B17)

claim_en: TARIFF SCOPE: ox and sheep ONLY — the redundancy geometry (the extra shor of the tail and seh of the head; without them shor-shor from Shabbat sweeps in every beast; tachtav-tachtav is spoken for by the payment-quality rule); kilayim IN via the o-ribbui against Rava's own binyan av; wild beast and birds OUT against both kal-vachomers; the WOMAN thief fully liable (yeshallem covers her — ish is reserved for the sale-clause below: a man is sold for his theft, a woman never).
source: BK 67b + Yalkut 342:4 (B24, B27); Mizrachi + Gur Aryeh + Siftei Chakhamim (B26-27); MdRShbY (B24)

claim_en: DISPOSAL CONDITIONS: u-tvacho ALL of it (partners who steal — one slaughtering without the other's assent exempts; sale minus 1/100th of slaughter-permitted parts = no fine; withheld wool/horns are NO remainder); sale IRREVERSIBLE like slaughter (30-day sale excluded); outside the owner's domain; benefit-permitted — and the act must not CAUSE the meat's prohibition (Shabbat-slaughter exempt because the knife itself forbids; tereifah liable — it was unfit before the knife; shechitah she-einah re'uyah SHMAH shechitah, against R. Shimon); nevelah-in-hand, nocher, me'aker excluded; tviha always means ritual slaughter.
source: Mishnah BK 7:5 + BK 68a-78b (B24); Meshekh Chokhmah 36 (B26); MdRShbY (B24); Hirsch :10 (B27)

claim_en: THE AGENCY EXCEPTION: slaughter-by-agent convicts the THIEF — the Torah's lone agent-for-sin liability, derived three ways (the hekesh from sale's inherent other-party; devei R. Yishmael from o; devei Chizkiyah from tachat) and FENCED by the two-verses-as-one rule (me'ilah + tviha-u-mchirah teach nowhere else); Hirsch dissolves all three 'exceptions' by personal status: the fine punishes THE CONTINUATION OF THE THEFT, and only the thief can continue his own theft — whoever holds the knife; the DECEIVED agent's act convicts the sender (Tosafot BK 79a; Shach contra); at the theft-act itself there is NO agency (the partner who helped carry after his sister's lifting walks — Rosh).
source: Kiddushin 43a + Ketubot 33b + BK 71a/79a (B24); Hirsch :5-:9 (B27); Tosafot BM 8a (B24); Rosh via Tur 348:11 (B25); Beit Yosef 348:6 Mordechai (B26)

claim_en: THE COMPOSED TARIFF: 4/5 CONTAINS the double + an increment, so where the double dies the whole fine collapses — hekdesh ('from the man's house, not the Temple's') and gentile owners ('his fellow') pay NOTHING of it: 'the Torah said four-and-five, not three-and-four'; five = FOUR AND IT (the tariff includes the principal; Prov 6:31's sevenfold = six and it); five half-oxen OK (partners' ox, confession to one partner — fines split; atonement doesn't: no half-kofer (half-ransom)); ownership condition: the thief who INHERITED or CONSECRATED then slaughtered kills HIS OWN — exempt (change-of-form acquisition: the stolen lamb grown to a ram is his); valuation timing: principal at theft-time, fines at TRIAL-time; payment quality: tachat-tachat — no five wasted beasts (each must STAND IN PLACE of the stolen one; MdRShbY counter-files tachat = money-value).
source: BM 57b + Shevuot 6:5 (B24); Mekhilta 'four and it' (B24); BK 71b (B24); MdRShbY ownership condition (B24); MT Theft 1:13-14 (B24); BK 67b negidin (B24)

claim_en: THE CONSTANTS' RATIONALE STACK: declared GEZERAT MELEKH ('a king's decree' — MdRShbY) yet derived four ways — R. Meir: base-4 = DOUBLE-OF-DOUBLE (he repeated the sin, the kefel doubles) +1 for the ox's lost labor; RYbZ: base-5 by decree, sheep discounted for the thief's self-degradation (kavod ha-briyot DISCOUNTS a fine); Kli Yakar: breeding ratios (ox sires 4 → 4+principal; the ram owes ELEVEN, dignity forgives seven = Prov 6:31's sevenfold); Kallah Rabbati: the Merciful pitied his TROUBLE (he had to carry it); plus the livelihood economics (the herd animal IS the man's life — beast-loss as mortal danger, Magen Avraham 248) and far-pasture deterrence (Moreh 3:41); the recidivism rationale (nishtaresh/shanah ba-chet) is the thief's own tam→mu'ad isomorphism.
source: MdRShbY (B24); BK 79b + Tosefta BK 7 (B24); Divrei David (B25); Aderet Eliyahu/Kli Yakar (B26); Kallah Rabbati 10:6 (B27); TT :1 (B24); Chatam Sofer mitzvah-pricing (B26)

claim_en: ENFORCEMENT: the fine is the COURT's (Hirsch: theft betrays the public trust guarding unwatched property; the owner has no claim to the fine) and SELF-CONFESSION KILLS IT — the self-convicted thief has restored the principle unasked (modeh biknas derived, not decreed; asher yarshi'un elohim — 'not the self-condemner'); confession exempts only in/before a proper court — TODAY no fines-courts exist, so NO confession exempts (Tur 348:8) and the fine is uncollectable (jurisdiction decay; the flying scroll of Zech 5 supplies the heavenly executor); strategic confession before arriving witnesses → principal only, and denying the slaughter denies no money (deposit-oath exempt, bitui-oath liable); collection ladder: movables → BEST land → self-sale (principal only, man only, only while Yovel runs, only if his value is swallowed by the theft).
source: Hirsch 21:37 (B26-27); BK 75 via SeMaG (B25); Tur CM 348:7-9 (B25); Shevuot 49a + MT Oaths 8:1 (B24); Hirsch Num 5:10 kefel-vs-chomesh (B27)

claim_en: THE MU'AD TEMPLATE AS SYSTEM-WIDE STATE MACHINE: the 3-then-vested pattern exported to PLAGUE (3 deaths in 3 days = epidemic threshold, Taanit), INSANITY (the shoteh classified by the gored-all-species rule, Chagigah 4a), MENSTRUAL VESTING (the 15th/16th/17th leaping cycle IS BK 37b's skipping ox — Chatam Sofer resolves the opposite directions by opposite presumptions: oxen presumed guarded, women presumed seeing), PENITENTIAL THEOLOGY (three sins forgiven — the fourth finds him forewarned, Yoma 86b), and the THIEF's own recidivism aggravation (BK 68a).
source: Bahya (B10); Chagigah 4a (B6); Chatam Sofer (B12); Tosafot Yom HaKippurim via PY (B17); TT :11 (B24)

claim_en: ROYAL AND DIVINE ACCOUNTABILITY THROUGH THE BLOCK'S OWN CLAUSES: King Yannai summoned to the Sanhedrin via ve-hu'ad BE-VA'ALAV ('a slave is as his owner's property' — the ox-arraignment clause reaches the throne; the judges' failure births 'a king neither judges nor is judged'); and God files HIMSELF under the block's damages law — 'I kindled the fire in Zion and I am bound to rebuild her' (the kindler-pays clause executed against Heaven); the two-Messiahs eschatology runs on the pit-clause (the fallen ox = Messiah b. Joseph, ve-ha-met yihyeh lo = his destined death, and the Pit's Owner repays — bar nafli).
source: Sanhedrin 19a via Ikar TYT (B3); Yalkut 345:3 (B22); Abarbanel Mashmia Yeshuah + Megalleh Amukkot (B15-16)
